evidence: Plin. NH 25.29: vetustissima inventū paeōnia est nōmenque auctōris retinet
terms.comment: Greek παιωνία, named, Pliny says, after the one who found it (Lewis & Short: Paeon). The long ō is Lewis & Short’s, against the short o of the region Paeonia. Pliny gives pentorobon and glycysidē as other names. Botanists keep the word for the genus Paeonia.

phrases.latin: vetustissima inventū paeōnia est nōmenque auctōris retinet
phrases.english: the peony was the first to be found, and keeps the name of its finder
